headline: CRUDE RETREATS; TRUMP-XI SUMMIT HANGS OVER BEANS
lead: Soybeans closed Friday at $13.03, down 7½ cents, and the fund liquidation was straightforward: nobody wanted to hold a long position into a weekend with the Trump-Xi summit on September 24 still unresolved. Wheat led the grain complex lower at $7.13, off 11½ cents.
teaser: Beans and wheat sold off Friday as the Trump-Xi summit looms. Crude had its worst week in months.

one_number.context: Saudi Aramco cutting European crude deliveries for October eased supply fears the market had over-priced. Brent fell below $105; diesel crack spreads are the real input-cost story going forward.

action: Unpriced new-crop beans: a Sept 24 Trump-Xi outcome below expectations is the sell signal; hold until then, not past it.

sections.title: GRAINS SELL INTO THE WEEKEND
sections.body: - Soybeans closed at **$13.03**, down 7½ cents, with ASA publicly urging Trump and Xi to address the 10% retaliatory levy still sitting on US beans at the Chinese border ahead of the September 24 summit.
sections.so_what: Beans are the summit trade. Everything else is noise until September 24.

sections.title: CRUDE RETREATS; DIESEL STILL TIGHT
sections.body: - WTI closed at **$95.47**, off 5.6% Friday, after Saudi Aramco confirmed it is rerouting roughly 60 million barrels through the Persian Gulf following damage to its East-West pipeline, killing the European supply scare that had crude bid all week.
sections.so_what: Fear premium gone; diesel crack spreads still hurt harvest budgets.

sections.title: CATTLE HOLD; FEEDERS UNDER PRESSURE
sections.body: - Live cattle closed at **$216.57**, up fractionally; the Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19 and still removing roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity, keeps packer margins as the binding constraint, not cattle numbers.
sections.so_what: Record-low placements plus a locked-out packer equals a cattle market that is not done tightening.

outside_the_pit.title: USDA Opens ARC/PLC Enrollment, Adds 30 Million Base Acres
outside_the_pit.body: USDA's first base-acre update in two decades adds more than 30 million acres to ARC and PLC eligibility.

watch_list.desc: Farm Bill floor scheduling: Senate Ag advanced 12-11; any procedural block before Sept 30 extension deadline matters.
Trump-Xi summit: beans above $13.15 on a confirmed purchase commitment, below $12.80 on a breakdown.
Weekly export sales: soybean sales under 700K MT keep the fund liquidation story in charge.

daily_quote.text: An economist is an expert who will know tomorrow why the things he predicted yesterday didn't happen today.

source_summary: CME Group Friday closes; USDA AMS; OilPrice.com; Feedstuffs; Drovers; Agri-Pulse; ASA
